answer: A stake-and-reputation bond resists sybils: each agent locks a deposit before it can transact, and good behavior builds a reputation score that gates larger deals. Creating a fresh identity means paying the deposit again and starting with zero reputation, so an attacker faces a steep, linear cost per fake agent while honest agents amortize one deposit over many trades. Like a tundra that only thaws slowly, reputation cannot be rushed; a spiral of fake endorsements collapses because endorsers risk their own bonds, and a single plume of suspicious activity triggers audits that slash the stake.
